Fold-switch pair 1nrjB_2gedB — 1nrjB vs 2gedB
Saccharomyces cerevisiae

Figure 1: Phylogenetic tree with per-cluster fold-preference heatmap.

The pair's MSA as a phylogenetic tree, one leaf per sequence cluster. Leaf rings show each cluster's predicted fold preference; the heatmap gives the seven analysed methods (AF2/AF3/ESMFold2/Boltz-2/BioEmu/ΔΔG/S4PRED) × clusters, followed by the two contact predictors (MSA-Transformer/CCMpred), which are shown for reference and enter no analysis; internal-node markers flag parsimony-inferred gain/loss/swap of fold state. Those markers come from four-state calls derived from the structure predictions, not from observations. The core question: do different groups of related sequences predict different folds? Clusters are tree-guided groups, not clades: only 12% are monophyletic across the dataset.

Figure 2: Aligned overlay (both folds superposed)

The single fold-switching chain of each fold superposed by TM-align; waters hidden, any ligand shown as green sticks. Grey = structurally conserved core, colour = divergent (fold-switching) region.

Figure 4: Best-cluster predicted contact maps over the two true folds.

Predicted contact maps (MSA-Transformer) for the clusters best matching each fold, over the true contacts of fold 1 (upper triangle) and fold 2 (lower). Divergent contacts between clusters are the contact-level signature of fold-switching.

Figure 5: Per-residue ΔΔG fold-preference contribution

ThermoMPNN per-residue contribution to the energetic fold preference: positive (red) = residues whose identity favors fold 1, negative (blue) = favor fold 2. Highlights which positions drive the fold choice.
